newsitem.title: USA: Connecticut treasurer outlines 1997 bond sales.
newsitem.headline: Connecticut treasurer outlines 1997 bond sales.

text.p: Connecticut's treasurer on Wednesday outlined a series of bond sales planned by the state during 1997, which include various different types of debt, such as general obligation and taxable bonds.
Christopher Burnham said that in August the state planned to sell from $250 million to $300 million of general obligations.
He made the comments during an interview with Reuters Financial Television, parts of which were scheduled to be shown on Thursday at 1515 EDT/1915GMT.

The sale of $100 million to $150 million of clean water bonds for the state revolving fund was planned in September, which would be followed by an offering in October of $150 million to $200 million of special transportation issues.
"We would anticipate that all three potentially could be on a negotiated basis," said Burnham.
He added that in December, Connecticut expected to sell around $75 million of taxable debt.
